title: ECDF and Mahalanobis Distance for Empirical Niche Modeling
text: first set simulations, assume environmental predictors describing species’ niche follow multivariate normal distribution. Dimensions pp range 1 5, sample sizes nn range 20 500 steps 20, mimicking increasing numbers occurrence records. combination pp nn, ecdf_compare_niche(): Draws fixed covariance matrix Σ\Sigma sampling Wishart distribution p+2p + 2 degrees freedom scale matrix set zero diagonal 1, ensuring positive-definite covariance (p,n)(p, n) combination. Generates 30 independent replicates nn records pp-variate normal distribution mean vector μp=𝟎\mu_p = \mathbf{0} (interpreted environmental optimum) covariance matrix Σ\Sigma. replicate, estimates sample mean μr\mu_r sample covariance Σr\Sigma_r computes squared Mahalanobis distance D2=(x−μr)⊤Σr−1(x−μr). D^2 = (x - \mu_r)^\top \Sigma_r^{-1} (x - \mu_r). Theoretical chi-squared suitability: Sχ2=1−Fχp2(D2), S_{\chi^2} = 1 - F_{\chi^2_p}(D^2),  Fχp2F_{\chi^2_p} cumulative distribution function chi-squared distribution pp degrees freedom. Empirical ECDF-based suitability: SECDF=1−FECDF(D2), S_{\text{ECDF}} = 1 - F_{\text{ECDF}}(D^2),  FECDFF_{\text{ECDF}} empirical cumulative distribution function distances. Calculates Pearson’s correlation coefficient Sχ2S_{\chi^2} SECDFS_{\text{ECDF}} replicate. setup mimics realistic ENM scenario multivariate means true covariances unknown must estimated occurrence records drawn correlated environmental space representing species’ theoretical niche (sensu Hutchinson 1978).
code: set.seed(1991) normal_res <- ecdf_compare_niche(   p_vals = 1:5,   n_vals = seq(20L, 500L, 20L),   n_reps = 30L )

title: Mahalanobis Distance Classifier for Ecological Niche Modeling — mahal.dist
text: model trained using presence-data estimate centroid covariance structure environmental conditions associated species occurrences. Suitability derived inverse tail probability Mahalanobis distance new observations estimated niche centroid. Two approaches available transform Mahalanobis distances probabilities: "chisq": assumes distances follow chi-squared distribution degrees freedom equal number predictors. "ecdf": uses empirical cumulative distribution function training distances, providing nonparametric estimate suitability. ECDF-based approach particularly useful assumption multivariate normality violated, common ecological data. model can used within caret::train() framework, enabling resampling, tuning, ensemble modeling workflows ecological niche modeling.

title: Mahalanobis Distance Classifier for Ecological Niche Modeling — mahal.dist
text: abs Logical. TRUE, predictions binarized using fixed threshold (default: 0.05). FALSE, class highest predicted probability returned. method Character. Method used convert Mahalanobis distances suitability values. Options "chisq" "ecdf".

title: Mahalanobis Distance Classifier for Ecological Niche Modeling — mahal.dist
text: Mahalanobis distance defines ellipsoidal niche environmental space. chi-squared formulation, suitability decreases distance niche centroid increases. ECDF formulation relaxes distributional assumptions estimating suitability directly empirical distribution distances observed presence data. Predictions return class probabilities "presence" "pseudoabsence", allowing flexible thresholding ensemble integration.

title: Mahalanobis Distance Classifier for Ecological Niche Modeling — mahal.dist

code: library(caret)  model <- train(   x = predictors,   y = response,   method = mahal.dist,   trControl = trainControl(classProbs = TRUE) ) library(caret)  grid <- expand.grid(   abs = c(TRUE, FALSE),   method = "ecdf" )  model <- train(   x = predictors,   y = response,   method = mahal.dist,   tuneGrid = grid,   trControl = trainControl(classProbs = TRUE) )
